title: How do we draw a figure on the isometric grid?
description: A block of two cubes is drawn on the isometric grid edge by edge. The board picks a starting corner, gives each edge a direction along the grid, counts the units of every edge, and erases the hidden lines.
teaching_notes: One idea: every edge of the figure is drawn along one of the three grid directions, one counted length at a time. Watch for students who draw slanted edges that do not follow the grid.

video_script.why: The child draws a figure on an isometric grid by choosing a start, giving each edge a grid direction and counting its units.
video_script.substitution: Draw each edge along height, length or depth, and count its units before moving on.
video_script.anchor: a block made of two cubes side by side, and an isometric grid with lines in three directions
video_script.payoff_line: Each figure is drawn edge by edge along the three grid directions, counting units

final_answer.value: Each figure is drawn edge by edge along the three grid directions, counting units
final_answer.spoken: each figure is drawn edge by edge along the three grid directions, counting units

hold_back: Answer: Each figure is drawn edge by edge along the three grid directions, counting units
never_show: an edge drawn off the grid lines marked as right
maths_rules: stand-in figure: a block of 2 cubes side by side, 2 units long, 1 unit deep, 1 unit tall
visible edges: 3 along the length of 2 units, 3 along the depth of 1 unit, 3 along the height of 1 unit
units of line: 3 x 2 + 3 x 1 + 3 x 1 = 6 + 3 + 3 = 12
video_script.design: The block of two cubes beside an isometric grid. A pencil starts at the near bottom corner and draws each edge along a grid direction, with the unit count shown beside it, until the hidden lines are erased.
open_questions: The figures of the book question are pictures that are not in the extracted text, so the video draws one block of two cubes and gives the method for any other figure.

<bookmark mark='sum'/>Three times two plus three times one plus three times one makes twelve units.
